references.text: The same command is repeated in Leviticus, where it states that an ox, sheep, or goat shall remain with its mother for seven days, and from the eighth day onward it may be accepted as a fire offering to the Lord.
It concerns that all firstborn males of cattle and small livestock are to be consecrated to the Lord, which relates to the requirement to give the firstfruits to God.
God commands that everything firstborn is to be consecrated to Him, both humans and animals, as background for the command to surrender the animal on the eighth day.
It repeats that all firstborn belong to the Lord, including the firstfruits of cattle and small livestock.
The firstborn of ox, sheep, and goat shall not be redeemed but is holy and must be offered to the Lord.
Jesus was circumcised on the eighth day, showing that the eighth day had special significance for consecration and dedication to God.
Complementary legal rule: The prohibition against slaughtering mother and offspring on the same day supports the requirement of seven days' stay with the mother.
